Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Town, shops & places

capital noun

the chief city of a country

also capital city, the capital, seat of government

classical

Liv. 1.16.7
Liv. 9.37.12: capita Etrūriae populōrum
Traupman 198, 203
M-O s.v. capital (seat of government)

caput, capitis n.

noun, third declension

a capital city

The head of a country or a people, usually with a genitive: Thebes was the head of all Greece (Nep. Epam. 10, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • urbs prīnceps — the capital city

    noun phrase: urbs with the adjective prīnceps · also used · modern · M-O s.v. capital, capital city, seat of government

  • mētropolis, mētropolis f. — a mother city; the chief city of a province

    noun, third declension · also used · late Latin · Cod. Just. 11.21 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. capital (seat of government)

    Greek μητρόπολις: a city that founded colonies, and in late Latin the chief city of a province (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • abī, nūntiā … Rōmānīs, caelestēs ita velle ut mea Rōma caput orbis terrārum sit

    go and tell the Romans that it is the will of heaven that my Rome be the capital of the worldLiv. 1.16.7

  • Quae urbs est caput?

    Which city is the capital?Traupman 198

See also city, state, province.
